title: Decoy: luring a piece to a bad square
outcomes: Finds the sacrifice that forces a piece onto a square where it can be attacked
Checks that the capture is forced and the follow-up wins at once
Says what makes the lure fail

steps.text: A **decoy** is a sacrifice that lures a piece, often the king, to a square where it can be hit. The opponent is better off taking, and the capture puts the piece where you want it. Ask: which piece do I want on which square, and what makes it go there?

steps.caption: Black to move. The white queen on e4 is defended by the king on e3. Other king moves lose to mate, so taking is White's best try.

line.say: The rook offers itself with check.
The king takes the rook and leaves e3.
The queen takes the queen with check.

claims.statement: ...Re2+ followed by ...Qxe4+ wins material along the engine line.
Only the king on e3 defends the queen on e4.

steps.text: A lure needs two things. **The capture must be forced**, or at least better than every other reply. **The follow-up must win at once** on the new square. If the opponent can decline, or another piece can take the offer, the sacrifice is just a lost piece.

steps.title: Another piece can take
steps.prompt: The white rook stands on d2 instead of d3, so it can take on e2 as well.

steps.text: **When it holds:** the offered piece must be taken and the lured piece lands where the follow-up wins. **When it fails:** the offer can be refused, the follow-up line is blocked, or the lured piece has a flight square. As a rule of thumb, check every reply that does not capture.

steps.prompt: Before you gave up a piece to lure another, did you check what happens if the offer is refused?
